statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 57 in the elevated band on a still-shut Saudi East-West pipeline, WTI near $100.05, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 85.6 percent for an increase. Confidence is 86 on a complete verified evidence set re-checked against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip that retraced in both directions. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about seventeen hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: under the fixed repository mapping it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A shut weekend tape: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range, NQ retraced a roughly 459-point round trip after firm core CPI, VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, and a Saudi pipeline outage still carrying no restart date, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping all travel toward a Sunday reopen beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a losing streak while still finishing the week lower. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, closing near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range against a 17.84 previous close.

The macro set behind that path is hawkish rather than disorderly. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both matching expectations, with core at 0.3% on the month, one tenth above consensus. CME FedWatch put the probability of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC at 85.6%, against 48.4% a month earlier. Treasury yields are firm, with the H.15 series showing the 2-year at 4.56%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37% as of the 10 September observation. A firm but broadly in-line print that still allowed a 459-point round trip is evidence of orderly price discovery, which is why the event raises Stress and not Tail.

The unresolved risks are in the Gulf and they are supply-route risks. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry shut the 7 million barrel per day East-West pipeline, the route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz toward the Red Sea, after drone attacks in the Riyadh and Madinah regions that Riyadh attributed to launches from Iraqi territory. That report was updated on 12 September and still carries no restart date, only a statement that further developments will be announced. Houthi forces completed a rapid push to control Yemen's entire Red Sea coast on Friday, taking Mocha, Dhubab and the island of Perim, also called Mayyun, at the Bab al-Mandeb entrance. Against that, two things qualify the escalation: the Houthi military spokesman said maritime navigation is safe for all companies except Saudi vessels, and oil eased rather than extended, with WTI settling near $100.05, down 2.37%, and Brent near $104.61, down 2.81%, after Iran confirmed it will meet Gulf foreign ministers and Iraqi representatives in Salalah, Oman on Monday to discuss Hormuz shipping. No new escalation was found in the hours since the previous assessment.

Cross-asset context from the shared collector is delayed, latest-session material and is used here as confirmation only, never as live price-path evidence. Its section coverage was partial this hour, with the calendar feed unavailable, so the calendar below rests on independently verified sources. What it does show is that Friday's advance was broad but internally dispersed: seven of eight tracked megacaps higher with a mean gain near 0.94%, semiconductors uneven with ARM up 4.17%, QCOM up 2.88% and NVDA fractionally lower, and Treasury futures modestly lower in line with firm yields. Dispersion of that kind is the opposite of the single-direction alignment that precedes mean-reversion failure.

The decisive fact for this horizon is mechanical. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about seventeen hours after the last slot of this forecast. Every one of the twenty-four forward hours therefore describes a market in which no Nasdaq-100 price can print, so no persistent one-way path, no failed retracement and no session extreme can form. Conditional Tail is held at a low residual floor that steps from 5 to 10 across the horizon, tracking accumulated unpriced weekend headline exposure ahead of an eventual reopen rather than any observed structure. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 06:00 UTC on 11 September to 05:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in a trend-up read through the European hours, with Tail between 13 and 15 as the advance extended. The 12:30 UTC inflation print produced the only elevated readings of the window, Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode with Confidence cut to 70 and then 80 while the post-release path was still forming. Tail fell back to 15 within ninety minutes as NQ retraced, held between 15 and 17 through the U.S. afternoon in mixed mode, then collapsed to 13 and 7 around the 21:00 UTC halt. The final eight slots sit at Tail 5 to 6 in normal mode, tracking the closure rather than a directional view, while Stress decayed steadily from 85 to 58 as the event passed and volatility fell.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about seventeen hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor for one more hour, then steps to 6 from 08:00 UTC, 7 from 14:00 UTC, 8 from 20:00 UTC, 9 from 00:00 UTC on Sunday and 10 in the final slot as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout. Stress runs 57 to 61 and describes the environment rather than a path: a Saudi East-West pipeline outage whose latest update still carries no restart date, WTI near $100.05, Houthi control of Yemen's Red Sea coast qualified by a statement that navigation is safe except for Saudi vessels, Monday's Salalah meeting on Hormuz shipping and a Wednesday policy decision priced near 85.6 percent for an increase. Confidence decays from 86 to a 78 floor as the verified evidence set ages without any live price path to refresh it. No danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one.
